chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Isma'il ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the one performing Tamattu' (Umrah then Hajj): if he comes, fulfills his Tamattu', and then the need arises for him to go to Medina, or to Dhat 'Irq, or to some of the mines, he said: 'He returns to Mecca with an Umrah, provided he is in a month other than the one in which he performed his Tamattu', because for every month there is an Umrah, and he is held hostage by his Hajj.'

I said: 'What if he entered in the same month he departed?' He said: 'My father was residing here, so he went out to meet some of these people, and when he returned and reached Dhat 'Irq, he entered into Ihram for Hajj from Dhat 'Irq, and entered [Mecca] while he was in Ihram for Hajj.'
And it is not permissible for anyone to enter Mecca except while in Ihram, and this has been permitted for the sick person who cannot endure it, and for the woodcutters.

key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعِ: One performing Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj with a break)
key_terms.ذَاتِ عِرْقٍ: Dhat 'Irq (a place near Mecca, often used as a Miqat)
key_terms.مُتْعَتَهُ: His Tamattu' (the state of being free from Ihram between Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.مُرْتَهَنٌ بِالْحَجِّ: Held hostage by Hajj (remaining in Ihram state)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a Mutamatti' pilgrerim who leaves Mecca after Umrah but before Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the status of the Mutamatti' who departs Mecca after Umrah, distinguishing between leaving in a different month (requiring a new Umrah) versus the same month (remaining in Hajj Ihram). This ruling underscores the principle that the Hajj obligation binds the pilgrim, preventing casual exit from the sacred precincts without proper ritual state. The text further reinforces the general rule that entry into Mecca requires Ihram, citing exceptions for the sick and woodcutters as recorded by al-Hattab.
